Work  /  American Heart Association
Event branding · Creative direction · Promotional materials

Most design has no scoreboard. A fundraiser does.

Event branding for the American Heart Association’s Boston Heart Ball and the Go Red For Women luncheon — one room, one evening, and a number at the end of it.

Client

American Heart Association

Services

Creative direction, brand strategy, visual design, event collaboration

Events

Boston Heart Ball · Go Red For Women

Engagement

Two consecutive years

Heart Ball — Cirque du Coeur. The invitation had to sit on a mantelpiece for months and still say black tie.
Go Red For Women, Boston Women’s Luncheon — February 2006.

The challenge

Heart disease is the leading cause of death for women, and most women do not know it. The Heart Ball and the Go Red For Women luncheon have to carry that fact and raise money on the same night — awareness and revenue, from one room, in a few hours.

A gala is also a crowded category. Every cause in the city is competing for the same tables, the same sponsors and the same evenings on the same calendar. The materials arrive months before the event and have to survive on a desk, in an inbox, and on a mantelpiece until the night itself.

Go Red for Women, February 2005. The dancer runs as a panelled grid across the invitation and the reply card — one image, cut apart and reassembled at each size.
“Good health is always in season.” The red dress mark carried the campaign across an evening that had to raise money and mean something.

The approach

Design the evening, not the invitation. A guest meets the event perhaps a dozen times — save-the-date, invitation, reply card, website, signage, program, table materials, auction, screen. Treated as separate jobs, twelve touchpoints produce twelve impressions. Treated as one system, they compound into a single argument by the time the ask is made.

Work inside the national identity, not around it. Go Red For Women is an established AHA campaign with its own equity. The task was not to reinvent it but to give the Boston events their own presence within it — recognizably part of the national movement, unmistakably a specific night in a specific city.

Replace with the actual creative decision — the image, the device, or the idea the two years were built on.

Hearts in Motion, May 2005. The grid became the system — invitation, reply card and table card all cut from it.
Boston Heart Ball ’05 — sponsorship kit, silent auction booklet and the ask. The pieces nobody photographs, and the ones that raise the money.

The outcome

The AHA came back the following year. For an organization that runs a competitive review on its flagship fundraiser, a second consecutive year is the verdict — the first year worked well enough that changing course was the greater risk.
